what: U6 first reads: what puts a lent film on a TV in the room, before any U6 row is written
screen: LG OLED55C2PUA (2022), webOS 22; on the WiFi at 192.168.1.11; advertises _airplay._tcp; no Cast receiver for video on this network (the one _googlecast._tcp device is a KEF LSX II speaker)
phone: iPhone at 192.168.1.3, Safari 26.6.1 (user agent iPhone OS 18_7, redirect.log)
clocks: redirect.log, jellyfin.log and jellyfin-conns.log are PDT (-07:00); airplay-page.node.log is UTC
short_address: http://192.168.1.4:8088/ answered 302 to the long address each read used, so nothing long was typed on a TV

reads.path: Safari on the iPhone opened the U4 House link on https://www.svrnme.sh/g/ (page at e7ba903), opened Sam's `film` lend (a plain <video controls> page, demo/runs/u4/2026-10-05/lend.mjs), AirPlay to the LG
reads.predicted_before: fails: the video's address is on the page's origin, which only the phone's service worker answers
reads.outcome: fail: the TV entered AirPlay and showed no video; the operator reported it looked audio only
reads.evidence: airplay-page.lend.log and airplay-page.node.log: the phone's worker read 49.4 MB through the relay, more than the 45.3 MB file (its first ranges overlap), mostly in 2 MiB ranges, 23:25:36Z-23:26:25Z (8.1 Mbit/s), then from the start again at 23:26:33Z; nothing reached the TV

reads.path: the LG's own web browser opened the same House link
reads.outcome: fail: the page said 'This browser could not open the page.' (web/app.js:235, the catch around init, the store and the join)
reads.evidence: redirect.log: user agent 'Chrome/87.0.3945.79 ... SmartTV/10.0'; the module parsed (it uses ??, Chrome 80+)
reads.cause: not reproduced here; by the published support tables, each of three stops it: the page's CSP admits wasm by 'wasm-unsafe-eval' (Chrome 97+, web/index.html:31); the wasm uses reference types (two tables, externref; Chrome 96+); the worker is a module (web/app.js:209, Chrome 91+)
reads.decision: operator, 2026-10-05: old TV browsers are not supported

reads.path: a scratch Jellyfin 12.0.0 (the macOS app's server, scratch dirs) on 192.168.1.4:8197, the test film in its library; jellyfin-web in Safari on the iPhone played it five times; AirPlay to the LG
reads.predicted_before: the TV plays, fetching the film from 192.168.1.4 itself
reads.outcome: fail: Cast reported unsupported (no Cast sender on iOS); AirPlay offered audio only; the LG never connected to :8197
reads.evidence: jellyfin.log (five starts, all 'Jellyfin Web' from 192.168.1.3); jellyfin-conns.log (only 192.168.1.3 until 16:46:38)
reads.cause: jellyfin-web 12.0.0 bundles hls.js, which prefers ManagedMediaSource and sets the video's disableRemotePlayback whenever it plays through it ('r.disableRemotePlayback=r.disableRemotePlayback||o&&a instanceof o' in the app's bundle); Safari then offers only the audio route

reads.path: Safari on the iPhone opened the film's own address on the scratch Jellyfin (/Videos/<id>/stream.mp4?Static=true, 206 video/mp4), no page, no worker, no MSE; AirPlay to the LG
reads.predicted_before: the TV plays, fetching the address itself
reads.outcome: fail: AirPlay said connected to the device; no video; the LG never connected to :8197
reads.cause: not determined: either iOS did not hand the TV the address or the TV did not fetch it; no control receiver was run

reads.path: 'Jellyfin for WebOS' 1.2.2 from the LG Content Store, server address 192.168.1.4:8197 typed once, signed in as the scratch user, played the test film
reads.predicted_before: the TV app plays from 192.168.1.4, and the phone's jellyfin-web lists the TV as somewhere to play
reads.outcome: pass for the first half: connected 16:46:38, signed in 16:46:55, playback 16:47:02-16:47:38 (29.9 s), DirectPlay; the operator: 'Yup that works'. The phone as remote was not exercised: no command to the TV's session is in the log
reads.evidence: jellyfin.log; jellyfin-conns.log (192.168.1.11 at 16:46:38); jellyfin-sessions.txt (the LG's session: SupportsRemoteControl true, SupportsMediaControl true, PlayMethod DirectPlay)

decision: operator, 2026-10-05: the screen is the app's own client; svrngs gives devices in the room reach to a lend across town through a member's computer on that network, and takes media on TVs and end-user devices out of its scope ('we're adding value, but we're not taking media on tvs and end user devices into our scope')
